newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania PM denies interior minister fled country.
newsitem.headline: Albania PM denies interior minister fled country.

text.p: Albania's interim Prime Minister Bashkim Fino, accusing President Sali Berisha of interfering in the running of government, on Wednesday denied that the interior minister had left the country and had to be replaced.
The interior ministry is a key post of state in Albania and has control of the police and other security forces.

Fino, appointed as prime minister on March 11 to lead a 10-party unity government ahead of Sunday's general election, rejected Berisha's order to replace Interior Minister Belul Celo, a member of Berisha's own Democratic Party, with another chief loyalist.
"Today, Mr Celo called his deputy minister saying he had not resigned and will be back in office to serve until the end of my government mandate," Fino told a news conference.
The post of interior minister was assigned to the Democrats in a March 9 deal after protracted negotiations over the ministerial shareout in the interim coalition government.

While the Socialists appear to have scored a decisive victory in the first round of a general election last Sunday, the interior ministry post has to remain in the hands of the Democrats until a new government is formed.
"There are only 10 to 15 days left until the new government will take over," he said.

Fino criticised Berisha's orders to deploy republican guardsmen -- whose duties are to protect the president, prime minister and the speaker of parliament -- to intervene in the operations of the police or interior ministry.
"I want to make clear that I will never allow anybody, including President Sali Berisha, to break the country's constitutional laws," Fino said.
Fino said interior ministry police, the Shik secret police and police special units were under his government's control.
"It is true that Berisha is still commander in chief of Albania's armed forces, but this does not mean he can break the rules," he said.
Fino said that to deploy armed forces, a president is obliged first to summon the Defence Council, of which Fino the interior and defence ministers are members.
